subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 22-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 6 hours after ingesting about 20 tablets of acetaminophen in a suicide attempt. He is alert but has nausea and right upper quadrant tenderness. His serum acetaminophen concentration is above the treatment line, serum transaminases are rising, and intravenous N-acetylcysteine is started.
question: Which of the following best explains the protective effect of this antidote?

options.text: It inhibits cytochrome P-450 2E1 and prevents formation of the reactive metabolite
It increases hepatic sulfation of acetaminophen
It increases renal excretion of unchanged acetaminophen
It replenishes hepatic glutathione, which detoxifies the reactive metabolite NAPQI
It directly reduces the reactive metabolite within mitochondria

explanation_correct: N-acetylcysteine provides cysteine, the rate-limiting amino acid for synthesis of the tripeptide glutathione. In acetaminophen overdose the glucuronidation and sulfation pathways are saturated, and cytochrome P-450 2E1 converts the excess drug to NAPQI; once glutathione is depleted, NAPQI binds cellular proteins and causes centrilobular hepatic necrosis. Restoring the glutathione pool allows NAPQI to be conjugated and excreted, which limits liver injury.

explanation_incorrect.A: N-acetylcysteine does not inhibit cytochrome P-450 2E1; it works by restoring the depleted glutathione pool rather than by blocking bioactivation.
explanation_incorrect.B: Sulfation is already saturated in overdose, and the principal protective effect of the antidote is glutathione repletion rather than increased sulfation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Renal excretion of unchanged acetaminophen is not the mechanism by which the antidote prevents hepatotoxicity.
explanation_incorrect.E: N-acetylcysteine does not directly reduce the reactive metabolite; it must first be used for glutathione synthesis before conjugation can occur.

educationalObjective: N-acetylcysteine limits acetaminophen hepatotoxicity by supplying cysteine for glutathione synthesis, allowing detoxification of the reactive metabolite NAPQI.
